attributes.morphology: coarse cleavage facets along dendrite branch axes

evidence.quote: in fractures of alloy ZhS6U-VI without hafnium additives the brittle component has the form of facets of coarse cleavages along the axes of dendrite branches at sites of segregation of eutectic carbides (Fig. le).
With growth of the hafnium content the amount and sizes of the brittle component in fractures of both alloys diminish (Fig. lb -d,f, g).
The effect of small hafnium additives on the change in the form of carbide seems to be caused by the high carbide-forming capacity of this element (several times higher than that of titanium [2]).
Consequently, hafnium additives promote growth of the crystallization rate of the alloys.
